cases.statement: Three affected siblings (P1 male, P2 female, P3 male) of consanguineous Pakistani parents, all homozygous; both parents carry the variant per segregation analysis (their zygosity is not stated explicitly). The review 42885896 lists the same three siblings again as Table S1 #117-119.

people.label: P1
people.key_phenotypes: global developmental delay, absent expressive language, limb hypotonia, microcephaly, febrile and afebrile seizures with atypical absences, dystonic movements, reduced/absent brain creatine peak on MRS

quotes.quote: Herein, we describe three siblings, currently aged 7 (P1, ♂), 5 (P2, ♀), and 3 (P3, ♂) years old, born to consanguineous parents, originating from Pakistan.

A normal pre‐ and perinatal history was reported, but during early infancy, they all showed significant global developmental delay (median age at unassisted walking: 28‐month‐old, range: 19–32‐month‐old), absent expressive language, limb hypotonia, pyramidal signs, ataxia, hyposomia, and microcephaly.
P1 also exhibited dystonic movements and suffered febrile and afebrile seizures.
P1 had initially presented, when 18‐month‐old, a prolonged febrile seizure with left head turning evolving to bilateral convulsive, followed by a prolonged post‐ictal right hemiparesis.
3T structural brain MRI did not show specific anomalies (Figure 1), though spectroscopy (MRS) revealed reduced/absent creatine peak in all patients (Figure 1).

people.label: P2
people.key_phenotypes: global developmental delay, absent expressive language, hypotonia, microcephaly, low plasma and urinary creatine, atypical absence seizures after supplementation start, reduced/absent brain creatine peak on MRS

quotes.quote: Thereafter, NGS sequencing of GAMT/AGAT/CT1 genes revealed a homozygous truncating variant in GAMT gene (NM_000156.6 (GAMT): c.438dup(p. His147Thrfs*44)).

A normal pre‐ and perinatal history was reported, but during early infancy, they all showed significant global developmental delay (median age at unassisted walking: 28‐month‐old, range: 19–32‐month‐old), absent expressive language, limb hypotonia, pyramidal signs, ataxia, hyposomia, and microcephaly.

GAMT‐D was first suspected in P2 because of low blood creatinine levels detected during an intercurrent infection at 2 years‐old; such findings in a child with developmental delay prompted to perform plasmatic and urinary creatine dosages, which were found to be abnormally low.
After 6 months of supplementation therapy, at 3 years, we captured brief atypical absences like P1 by video‐EEG monitoring (Figure 3A), as well as interictal irregular spike‐and‐wave discharges.
3T structural brain MRI did not show specific anomalies (Figure 1), though spectroscopy (MRS) revealed reduced/absent creatine peak in all patients (Figure 1).

people.key_phenotypes: global developmental delay, absent expressive language, hypotonia, microcephaly, no seizures (early supplementation), reduced/absent brain creatine peak on MRS

phenotype_specificity.statement: Features typical of GAMT deficiency as the paper describes it (developmental delay, epilepsy, movement disorder), with low plasma/urinary creatine and reduced/absent brain creatine on MRS in all three siblings. Testing was a three-gene panel (GAMT/AGAT/CT1); no broader exclusion of other genes is reported. Plasma GAA values are not reported.

quotes.quote: GAMT‐D was first suspected in P2 because of low blood creatinine levels detected during an intercurrent infection at 2 years‐old; such findings in a child with developmental delay prompted to perform plasmatic and urinary creatine dosages, which were found to be abnormally low.
Thereafter, NGS sequencing of GAMT/AGAT/CT1 genes revealed a homozygous truncating variant in GAMT gene (NM_000156.6 (GAMT): c.438dup(p. His147Thrfs*44)).
3T structural brain MRI did not show specific anomalies (Figure 1), though spectroscopy (MRS) revealed reduced/absent creatine peak in all patients (Figure 1).

segregation.statement: Three affected siblings are homozygous; segregation analysis showed maternal and paternal inheritance. No unaffected siblings are reported as tested. Family history negative for neurological disorders.

quotes.quote: The analysis was then extended to her siblings, confirming the same homozygous variant; segregation analysis showed both maternal and paternal inheritance.
Herein, we describe three siblings, currently aged 7 (P1, ♂), 5 (P2, ♀), and 3 (P3, ♂) years old, born to consanguineous parents, originating from Pakistan.
Family history was negative for neurological disorders.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: 1-bp duplication in coding exon 4 causing a frameshift, predicted p.(His147ThrfsTer44) (from the HGVS). The authors state it yields a truncating transcript and loss of function, which they call a known disease mechanism (stated, not assayed).

quotes.quote: This is a novel frame‐shift variant in exon 4 affecting the functional domain “RMT2”; it results in a truncating transcript and loss of function of the protein, that is a known mechanism of the disease.

authors_classification.statement: 40543028: Likely Pathogenic (PVS1, PM2). The review 42885896 states no variant classification; it says it excluded patients with VUS or likely benign variants (cohort-level inclusion rule).

quotes.quote: Review, classification, and interpretation of the variant were made according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMGG) guidelines (Likely Pathogenic, PVS1, PM2).
During data extraction, duplicate cases were consolidated, and patients harboring variants of uncertain significance (VUS) or likely benign variants were excluded (e.g., PMID: 37228909).

concerns: Same persons under two identities: 42885896 Table S1 #117, #118 and #119 cite 'Schifino 2025 Pt 1/2/3, PMID: 40543028', so GAMT-ID0265, GAMT-ID0266 and GAMT-ID0267 are the same individuals as GAMT-ID0062, GAMT-ID0063 and GAMT-ID0064 (sex and ages match). They add no independent case.
All three affected carriers are siblings from one consanguineous family; the evidence is a single family.
Parents' zygosity is not stated in words; the paper says only that segregation showed maternal and paternal inheritance.
Testing was a GAMT/AGAT/CT1 panel; no exome or wider gene exclusion is reported.
The authors call the variant novel and cite a population criterion, but give no population data in the paper.
notes_for_panel: Single consanguineous family (three homozygous affected siblings). The authors' own ACMG call is quoted under authors_classification (40543028). 42885896 only re-lists the same siblings in its pediatric review table.
